c74object.name: evi.biquadcoeff~
c74object.digest: Audio rate biquad coefficients calculator with selection of 40 different filter types.
c74object.description:
evi.biquadcoeff~ is a 'max define' for the evi_biquad_coeff.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.biquadcoeff~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
evi.biquadcoeff~ is an audio rate coefficients calculator for the biquad~ (or evi.biquad~) object. High level filter parameters are frequency, gain and Q. The units used for frequency and gain can be set via attributes.

inlet.description: Cutoff in Hz (default) or Pitch (change units with 'cutoffunits' attribute).
Gain in dB (default) or linear value (change units with 'gainunits' attribute).
Q of currently selected filter type, typically clamped 0.1..18, but some filter types can take much higher values (e.g. 'reson' or 'bp')

attribute.name: cutoffunits
attribute.description: Set the units for the cutoff frequency inlet (inlet 1). 0 = in Hz (default), 1 = in Pitch (e.g. 0..127).

attribute.name: filter
attribute.description: Set the filter type by integer index: 0=bypass, 1=lowpass, 2=highpass, 3=bandpass, 4=bandstop, 5=peaknotch, 6=lowshelf, 7=lowshelfcookbook, 8=highshelf, 9=highshelfcookbook, 10=resonant, 11=bp, 12=allpass, 13=gainlpass, 14=gainhpass, 15=gainbpass, 16=gainbstop, 17=gainresonant, 18=gainbp, 19=gainapass, 20=lowpassanalog1, 21=lowpassanalog2, 22=highpassanalog, 23=bandpassanalog, 24=gainbpassanalog, 25=notchanalog, 26=peaknotchanalog1, 27=peaknotchanalog2, 28=lowshelfanalog1, 29=lowshelfanalog2, 30=highshelfanalog1, 31=highshelfanalog2, 32=resonantanalog, 33=butterlowpass, 34=butterhighpass, 35=butterbandpass, 36=butterbandreject, 37=buttergainlpass, 38=buttergainhpass, 39=buttergainbpass, 40=buttergainbreject

attribute.name: gainunits
attribute.description: Set the units for the gain inlet (inlet 2). 0 = in linear amplitude, 1 = in dB (the default).

c74object.discussion: For a complete list of the available filter types (by index) double-click the abstraction and look at the comments at the top of the code block. For more information about biquads and other filter types in evieve see the 'evieve biquad' tab of the helpfile.
